results.title: Reproducing Inequality? Social Capital, Digital Literacy, and SES in ...
results.content: With a focus on the roles of digital literacy and socioeconomic status (SES), this study examines the influence of social capital on China’s high school graduates’ access to higher education. The results indicate that while social capital positively correlates with access to higher education across all groups, its advantages are more pronounced among high SES students, especially regarding entrance to elite universities. results.title: [PDF] Sociological barriers to equitable digital learning - CRR Publishers
results.content: This lack of access to technology creates significant barriers to educational equity, as students in these areas cannot fully benefit from digital learning opportunities. Students with limited social and cultural capital may struggle to access and benefit from digital learning platforms, widening the educational achievement gap. The lack of high-speed internet in rural areas is a significant barrier, making it difficult for students to access digital learning resources, participate in virtual classes, and complete online assignments. This trend highlights the importance of addressing systemic educational inequalities and ensuring that all students, regardless of their racial or ethnic background, have equitable access to digital learning opportunities. Students from higher socioeconomic backgrounds often have more outstanding social capital, which provides them with better access to technology and support for digital learning.
